Title: Learning-based Query Performance Modeling and Prediction
Problem: Can learned models predict query latency better than analytical cost models?
Method: Plan-level and operator-level learned models, plus a hybrid, static features only
Main Result: Learned models outperform analytical cost models for latency; hybrid trades accuracy for generality
Limitation: Contradicted by the 2013 calibration work; static/dynamic split
Research Gap: The pro-ML pole of the debate Option B would be entering
Relevance to my research: Defines the debate FinCluster's RQ1 sits inside. FinCluster's result lands on the anti-ML side.

Title: Predicting query execution time: Are optimizer cost models really unusable?
Problem: Is ML necessary to predict query execution time?
Method: Calibrated optimizer cost model vs published ML predictors; cardinality refinement
Main Result: A properly calibrated analytical cost model is competitive with and often better than the best reported ML results
Limitation: Database queries only; needs optimizer internals; no synthetic-generator analysis
Research Gap: Establishes that a non-ML baseline can beat ML at execution-time prediction, but on a genuinely hard task
Relevance to my research: STRONGEST PRIOR AGAINST OPTION B. The headline claim of Option B is already made here, in 2013, at ICDE.

Title: Robust estimation of resource consumption for SQL queries using statistical techniques
Problem: Do statistical resource-estimation models generalise beyond their training workload?
Method: Statistical models for SQL resource consumption, tested for robustness
Main Result: Proposed approaches lack robustness and do not generalise well to unseen queries
Limitation: Resource consumption rather than wall-clock service time
Research Gap: Generalisation failure of learned performance models is documented
Relevance to my research: Relevant to the leakage/generalisation argument, and to why grouped splitting matters.

Title: Towards predicting query execution time for concurrent and dynamic database workloads
Problem: Predicting execution time for dynamic concurrent workloads
Method: Optimizer cost model plus queueing and buffer-pool model, compared against an ML variant
Main Result: Analytic modelling gives competitive and often better accuracy than the ML counterpart
Limitation: Database-specific; assumes optimizer cost model is available
Research Gap: Second independent demonstration that analytical models beat ML here
Relevance to my research: SECOND STRONGEST PRIOR AGAINST B. Also a precedent for queue modelling, so partly supports C.

Title: A Machine Learning Approach to SPARQL Query Performance Prediction
Venue: 2014 IEEE/WIC/ACM International Joint Conferences on Web Intelligence (WI) and Intelligent Agent Technologies (IAT)
Problem: SPARQL query performance prediction without data statistics
Method: Query feature vectors, k-NN regression and nu-SVR
Main Result: Accurate prediction without underlying RDF statistics
Research Gap: Feature-vector framing of queries
Relevance to my research: Another instance of the same comparison template; supports the crowding argument.

Title: Uncertainty aware query execution time prediction
Problem: Point predictions hide prediction uncertainty
Method: Treats selectivities and cost constants as random variables to infer an error distribution
Main Result: Estimated prediction errors correlate strongly with actual errors
Research Gap: Uncertainty reporting is established practice that FinCluster does not yet do
Relevance to my research: Methodological gap in FinCluster: only point MAE/RMSE are reported, no uncertainty.

Title: Same Queries, Different Data: Can We Predict Runtime Performance?
Problem: Predicting runtime for fixed query sets over varying input data
Method: Per-segment ML estimates composed into a global analytical model
Main Result: Under 25 percent error for 90 percent of predictions using minimal input statistics
Research Gap: Fixed-workload/varying-data setting is close to FinCluster's fixed-processor/varying-transaction setting
Relevance to my research: Structurally the closest analogue to the FinCluster experimental design.

Title: Quick Execution Time Predictions for Spark Applications
Problem: Fast execution-time estimates for Spark applications under varying resources
Method: Lightweight predictive models over executor cores and data size
Main Result: Enables schedulers to configure applications for a target execution time
Research Gap: Resource-count as an input feature, analogous to FinCluster's node profile
Relevance to my research: Parallel to FinCluster's node_profile feature; useful for framing node capacity as a predictor.

Title: Contender: A Resource Modeling Approach for Concurrent Query Performance Prediction
Problem: Predicting query performance under concurrency
Method: Resource-contention modelling with Concurrent Query Intensity metrics; low training requirement
Main Result: Effective predictions for both static and dynamic concurrent workloads
Limitation: Analytical workloads; no learned routing policy
Research Gap: Concurrency-aware performance prediction predates FinCluster's queue-aware idea
Relevance to my research: IMPORTANT FOR OPTION C. Prior art for predicting under contention rather than in isolation.

Title: Stage: Query Execution Time Prediction in Amazon Redshift
Problem: Production execution-time prediction with cold-start and drift problems
Method: Predictor deployed in Amazon Redshift for admission, scheduling, resource control
Main Result: Addresses cold start and robustness against workload/data change
Research Gap: Shows the task is live and unsolved in production, not a toy problem
Relevance to my research: Evidence that execution-time prediction has real operational value - supports the premise, not the novelty.

Title: Runtime prediction of high-performance computing jobs based on ensemble learning
Problem: Predicting HPC job runtime for backfill scheduling
Method: Ensemble learning over job logs from three real HPC systems
Main Result: LightGBM gives higher accuracy and faster computation than compared models
Research Gap: Model-comparison studies on real logs are standard and well populated
Relevance to my research: Shows the model-comparison genre is saturated - reinforces that Option B's RQ1 form adds little.

Title: PREP: Predicting Job Runtime with Job Running Path on Supercomputers
Problem: User-supplied runtime estimates are overestimated, harming backfilling
Method: Job running path features from historical logs
Main Result: Improves runtime prediction over prior log-feature approaches
Research Gap: Prediction feeding a scheduling decision
Relevance to my research: Precedent for the prediction-then-scheduling pipeline FinCluster proposes.

Title: Execution Time Prediction for Cypher Queries in the Neo4j Database Using a Learning Approach
Problem: Execution time prediction for graph queries
Method: Learned model over Cypher query features on Neo4j
Main Result: SQL-oriented QPP methods do not transfer directly to Cypher
Research Gap: Shows QPP methods are re-derived per engine
Relevance to my research: Demonstrates the field's habit of re-running the same comparison in a new setting - which is what Option B risks being.

Title: Application of Machine Learning Algorithms for the Query Performance Prediction
Venue: Advances in Electrical and Computer Engineering
Problem: Relationship between system load/throughput and query response time in OLTP
Method: ML algorithms over a real OLTP system
Main Result: Load and throughput are central to response time in short-transaction systems
Research Gap: Load-dependence of response time in transactional systems
Relevance to my research: DIRECTLY SUPPORTS OPTION C: in real transaction systems, response time is driven by load, not just transaction content.

Title: KVM, Xen and Docker: A performance analysis for ARM based NFV and cloud computing
Problem: Performance comparison of virtualisation and container technologies
Method: Benchmark suite across KVM, Xen, Docker on ARM
Main Result: Quantifies container versus hypervisor overhead
Research Gap: Container overhead characterisation is long established
Relevance to my research: Background for why container measurement needs care; not a novelty threat.

Title: Rusty: Runtime Interference-Aware Predictive Monitoring for Modern Multi-Tenant Systems
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
Problem: Predicting workload sensitivity to interference in multi-tenant containers
Method: Runtime observability and forecasting of interference effects
Main Result: Finer-grained interference modelling than prior coarse-grained approaches
Research Gap: Interference prediction is mature; controlled measurement of it is less so
Relevance to my research: Nearest neighbour on the systems side; shows the community FinCluster should target.

Title: CloudScope: Diagnosing and Managing Performance Interference in Multi-tenant Clouds
Problem: Lightweight diagnosis of interference in multi-tenant clouds
Method: Discrete-time Markov chain model of interference
Main Result: Interference diagnosis without heavy micro-benchmarking or online training
Research Gap: Analytical interference modelling precedent
Relevance to my research: Shows analytical modelling is a live alternative to ML in this domain too.

Title: Evaluating the impact of fine-scale burstiness on cloud elasticity
Problem: Does fine-scale workload burstiness change measured elasticity?
Method: Workload models reproducing empirical burstiness; experimental case study
Main Result: Fine-scale burstiness materially affects elasticity measurements
Research Gap: Benchmark realism affects measured outcomes
Relevance to my research: Supports the general argument that generator design determines measured results - conceptually adjacent to FinCluster's finding.

Title: Machine Learning based Interference Modelling in Cloud-Native Applications
Problem: Predicting interference before co-locating containers
Method: ML models over co-located container workloads
Main Result: Interference level can be predicted before sharing a VM
Limitation: Prediction target is interference, not service time
Research Gap: Pre-placement prediction is established
Relevance to my research: Close to FinCluster's routing premise, using interference instead of service time.

Title: Performance interference of co-allocated applications: a systematic literature review
Problem: Systematic review of performance interference in co-allocated applications
Method: Systematic literature review of prediction/analysis techniques and input metrics
Main Result: Maps the techniques, metrics and tools used across the field
Research Gap: Provides the field map FinCluster's related-work section needs
Relevance to my research: Best single entry point for positioning FinCluster in the systems literature.

Title: Characterizing Container Performance in Edge Computing
Problem: Docker overhead characterisation on constrained edge hardware
Method: Micro and macro benchmarks on Raspberry Pi nodes
Main Result: Spin-up delays for short tasks, isolation/performance trade-offs
Research Gap: Container measurement characterisation continues to be published
Relevance to my research: Recent evidence that container measurement studies remain publishable.

Title: Investigating the Impact of Isolation on Synchronized Benchmarks
Problem: Which isolation mechanism makes cloud benchmarking reliable under contention?
Method: Compares cgroups plus CPU pinning, Docker containers, and Firecracker microVMs against an unisolated baseline with a noise generator
Main Result: Process isolation lowered false positives; Docker containers were MORE susceptible to noise despite using cgroups and pinning internally
Limitation: Duet benchmarking context; no prediction task
Research Gap: cgroups plus CPU pinning as a benchmark isolation strategy is already evaluated
Relevance to my research: STRONGEST PRIOR AGAINST FINCLUSTER'S PROTOCOL NOVELTY. The exact mechanism combination FinCluster arrived at in v0.6 is already published, and this paper finds Docker specifically weaker.

Title: Does Linux Provide Performance Isolation for NVMe SSDs? Configuring cgroups for I/O Control in the NVMe Era
Problem: Whether cgroup configuration actually delivers storage performance isolation
Method: Systematic evaluation of cgroup configurations for NVMe SSDs
Main Result: No uniform configuration achieves isolation across properties; trade-off with utilisation
Research Gap: cgroup isolation is imperfect and this is documented for storage
Relevance to my research: The storage analogue of FinCluster's CPU throttling finding - shows this style of result is publishable but also already being done.

Title: Real-Time Interference-Aware CPU and I/O Capping Mechanism for Multi-Tenant Containers
Problem: Maintaining QoS under contention in multi-tenant containers
Method: Real-time interference-aware CPU and I/O capping mechanism
Main Result: Conventional static capping is insufficient under high contention
Limitation: Mechanism paper, not a measurement-methodology paper
Research Gap: Dynamic capping as an alternative to static quotas
Relevance to my research: Suggests FinCluster's static-quota node model is a simplification reviewers may question.

Title: Shortcut to Nowhere: Demystifying Deep Spurious Regression
Problem: Spurious correlations in CONTINUOUS regression targets, not classification
Method: Defines Deep Spurious Regression; exploits similarity among spurious attributes in label and feature space
Main Result: Fills the benchmark and technique gap for spurious correlation in continuous prediction
Limitation: Evaluated on computer vision, environmental sensing and LLM regression - NOT systems
Research Gap: Spurious regression is now named and benchmarked, but never in a systems/performance-prediction setting
Relevance to my research: CLOSEST CONCEPTUAL PRIOR TO FINCLUSTER'S FINDING, and simultaneously the clearest evidence that the systems instance is unoccupied.

Title: SynQL: A Controllable and Scalable Rule-Based Framework for SQL Workload Synthesis for Performance Benchmarking
Problem: Existing benchmarks offer too few fixed templates for statistical generalisation
Method: Deterministic schema-graph traversal to synthesise diverse executable SQL workloads
Main Result: Produces near-maximally diverse workloads where fixed templates and LLM generation fail
Limitation: SQL domain; proposes a generator rather than diagnosing a degenerate one
Research Gap: The problem FinCluster hit - a generator too template-bound to support generalisation - is acknowledged, but as motivation for a better generator, not as a measured failure
Relevance to my research: MOST IMPORTANT SINGLE PAPER FOR THE NOVELTY BOUNDARY. It states the premise; FinCluster measures the consequence.

Title: AGILE: elastic distributed resource scaling for Infrastructure-as-a-Service
Problem: Scaling resources ahead of demand without application knowledge
Method: Wavelet-based medium-term resource demand prediction
Main Result: Enough lead time to start instances before SLO violation
Research Gap: Prediction horizon and lead time as design parameters
Relevance to my research: Highly cited anchor for prediction-driven resource decisions.

Title: SLO-Aware Inference Scheduler for Heterogeneous Processors in Edge Platforms
Venue: ACM Transactions on Architecture and Code Optimization
Problem: Mapping concurrent ML inference to heterogeneous edge processors under SLOs
Method: SLO-aware scheduling across GPU, DSP and accelerators
Main Result: Scheduling heterogeneous computation under constrained budgets
Research Gap: Heterogeneous-processor scheduling with predicted cost
Relevance to my research: Precedent for routing across heterogeneous nodes using predicted execution cost - Option C's core mechanism.

Title: Predicting the End-to-End Tail Latency of Containerized Microservices in the Cloud
Problem: Predicting end-to-end tail latency of containerised microservice workflows
Method: ML over resource metrics from multiple cloud layers; KVM, Docker, Kubernetes on Chameleon
Main Result: High prediction accuracy even under multi-tenant interference
Limitation: Sock Shop benchmark; no routing policy evaluated
Research Gap: Latency prediction in containers is established; using it to route is less so
Relevance to my research: DEFINES OPTION C'S ACADEMIC HOME. Closest venue-and-community match for FinCluster.

Title: QoS-Aware Co-Scheduling for Distributed Long-Running Applications on Shared Clusters
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
Problem: Co-scheduling long-running containerised applications on shared clusters
Method: QoS-aware co-scheduling accounting for latency propagation across microservices
Main Result: Detects and mitigates QoS violations under network and dependency uncertainty
Research Gap: Queue and dependency effects dominate at system level
Relevance to my research: Supports Option C's premise that queueing, not service time, drives system outcomes.

Title: IRIS: Interference and Resource Aware Predictive Orchestration for ML Inference Serving
Problem: Interference- and resource-aware scheduling of ML inference in the cloud
Method: Predictive inference scheduling framework
Main Result: Balances QoS against operator cost under interference
Research Gap: Prediction-driven placement is an active area
Relevance to my research: Direct competitor framing for Option C; shows the baseline set reviewers will expect.

Title: Adrias: Interference-Aware Memory Orchestration for Disaggregated Cloud Infrastructures
Problem: Orchestration for disaggregated cloud infrastructure under interference
Method: Deep learning over low-level performance events
Main Result: Additional scheduling knobs for disaggregated resources
Research Gap: Low-level event features for orchestration
Relevance to my research: Peripheral; included to map the orchestration community.

Title: Niyama: Node scheduling for cloud workloads with resource isolation
Venue: Concurrency and Computation Practice and Experience
Problem: Protecting latency-sensitive tasks from CPU bandwidth contention
Method: Modified deadline scheduling with estimated deadlines per interval
Main Result: Secures CPU bandwidth for latency-sensitive tasks without explicit deadlines
Research Gap: CPU bandwidth contention handled at scheduler rather than quota level
Relevance to my research: Alternative to FinCluster's quota-based node emulation; a reviewer may ask why quotas were chosen.

Title: From distributed tracing to proactive SLO management: a mini-review of trace-driven performance prediction for cloud-native microservices
Problem: Moving from post-hoc analysis to predicting SLO risk before a request finishes
Method: Mini-review of trace-based proactive SLO management
Main Result: Queue buildup and downstream slowdown propagate to tail latency; early warning from partial traces
Research Gap: Predicting completion before a request finishes is an active industrial demand
Relevance to my research: STRONGLY SUPPORTS OPTION C's target choice - completion time predicted from observable pre-completion state.
